name: repeat_calls_while_counter_nonzero
description: Tests a global word and optionally calls a subroutine, then runs a loop of four subroutine calls that repeats while a 16-bit counter is non-zero. The only branch logic is the global test and the loop counter.

name: load_view_after_two_calls
description: Calls two subroutines, then invokes graphics.LoadView through the graphics library base. It is a setup step that switches the display view after its helper calls.

name: load_view_after_one_call
description: Calls one subroutine, then invokes graphics.LoadView through the graphics library base. It is the shorter variant of the view switch that follows two helper calls.

name: step_packed_nibbles_toward_target
description: Walks a buffer backwards, moving each low nibble one step toward the matching nibble in a second buffer, and moving the high nibble one step on odd offsets only. It stores the recombined byte back into the first buffer.

name: clear_word_when_counter_zero
description: Makes two subroutine calls, then either calls one more and returns, or when the counter is zero clears the word at structure field 702 in register A6. The zero-clear branch is the only direct memory write.

name: decrement_rgb_nibbles_in_table
description: Copies eight longwords from a table pointed to by the structure field at offset 1200 into a global buffer. It then decrements each non-zero 4-bit field of each of the eight colour words, treating the three fields as the blue, green and red nibbles.

name: interpolate_colour_word_and_store
description: Scales the per-channel differences between two 4-bit colour words by a factor, divides by 15 to blend them, and stores the result in two palette tables. It calls a follow-up subroutine when the word at structure field 170 is non-negative or the word at structure field 230 is zero.

name: clear_rectangle_in_four_bitplanes
description: Zeroes a rectangular block of words in four bitplanes whose planes are 8000 bytes apart. The row start address is taken from a lookup table indexed by the top row, and the width and height come from structure fields.

name: forward_bitmap_blit_call
description: Calls BltBitMap through the graphics library base without setting up arguments in this routine. It relies entirely on the caller's registers, so it is a thin pass-through.

name: invoke_bitmap_blit
description: Calls BltBitMap through the graphics library base with no argument setup in this routine. It is the same pass-through as its neighbour, reached from a different caller.

name: blit_bitmap_from_data_pointer
description: Calls BltBitMap through the graphics library base, reached via a pointer stored in the hunk data. It is a thin pass-through and is entered from the data table rather than from code.

name: blit_bitmap_single_call
description: Calls BltBitMap through the graphics library base as its only action. It is a thin pass-through used by one caller.

name: advance_cycling_counter_word
description: Adds three to a global word, wrapping it back to a negative start value of minus 78 once it passes 251. It calls a subroutine first when the word is out of its expected range.

name: copy_rectangle_across_four_bitplanes
description: Copies a rectangular block of words from a source area to a destination area in four bitplanes spaced 8000 bytes apart. Source and destination row addresses come from a lookup table indexed by the row offsets.

name: blit_when_coordinate_below_limit
description: Calls BltBitMap through the graphics library base only when the input word is less than 198 and not equal to it. Otherwise it returns without drawing.

name: blit_when_value_positive
description: Calls BltBitMap through the graphics library base only when the input word is greater than zero. Otherwise it returns without calling the blit.

name: clip_rectangle_to_bounds
description: Clamps a rectangle's horizontal and vertical extent against four bounds stored in the structure at A6. It returns the two clip amounts packed into one 64-bit result, and exits early when a clipped size becomes zero.

name: blit_helper_result_twice
description: Calls a helper routine to obtain a value, passes that value to BltBitMap through the graphics library base, then makes a second BltBitMap call. Both calls go through the same library vector.

name: blit_helper_result_once_more
description: Calls a helper routine to obtain a value, then makes BltBitMap calls through the graphics library base. Its code matches the preceding routine, so the two differ only in where they sit in the file.

name: read_dos_and_return_byte
description: Calls dos.Read through the DOS library base and returns the byte stored in the global variable. The read result itself is not returned; the caller receives the global byte.

name: reset_audio_volumes_and_wait
description: Calls four helper routines, then zeroes the shared global word four times and loops on a fixed-count wait. The facts list the four audio channel volume registers as touched, so this is the audio volume reset step.

name: forward_single_helper_call
description: Calls one subroutine and returns, with no state of its own. It is a thin wrapper around that helper.

name: start_audio_channel_dma
description: When the flag at structure field 756 is zero, sets up one audio channel's pointer and length registers and waits for the display frame twice through the graphics library when a shifted mask is non-zero. It then writes the channel's DMA and interrupt enable bits.

name: set_audio_channel_without_wait
description: When the flag at structure field 756 is zero, sets up one audio channel's pointer and length registers and stores the sample values into shared globals. Unlike its neighbour it skips the frame wait, then writes the DMA and interrupt enable bits.

name: trigger_channels_from_mask
description: When the flag at structure field 756 is zero, calls helper routines once for each set bit in a channel mask, with the first helper's value taken from another register. It then stores the mask and its parameters into shared globals.

name: busy_wait_delay_loop
description: Counts a 16-bit word down from 21000 to minus one with no other work, acting as a fixed busy-wait delay.

name: select_lowest_set_channel
description: When the flag at structure field 756 is zero, finds the lowest set bit of a channel mask by shifting it. It stores the matching table entry as the current channel parameter and sets the state value to two.

name: update_audio_channel_periods
description: Computes a scaled period from the current state and copies it into the shadow period variable of each enabled channel, which the facts show as the four audio period registers. It advances the state when the period reaches its target.

name: set_channel_bit_mask
description: Stores a one-bit DMA channel mask in the shared global word, with the bit position taken from the input register. It is the channel selector used by the DMA control code.

name: initialise_state_and_flags
description: Calls four helper routines, then zeroes several fields of the structure at A6 and of shared globals. It copies one pointer-sized value into a structure field and sets a flag word to one.

name: skip_spaces_then_read_command
description: Reads characters through a helper until one is not a space. When that character is the letter g it enables a flag, reads until a zero byte, then clears the flag, and in both cases sets the shared global word to all ones.

name: read_until_nonzero_byte
description: Sets a flag, reads through a helper until it returns a non-zero byte, then clears the flag and sets a shared global word to all ones.

name: advance_sequencer_tick
description: Steps the sequencer one tick: when a step counter is due it loads the next table entries, updates the envelope-like values for two voices, and calls a helper to apply each active voice's period. It also handles a timed table index.

name: clear_flag_return_stack_value
description: Clears the shared flag word and returns the value passed on the stack unchanged.

name: select_table_entry_pointer
description: Looks up a 4-byte offset in a table using a value from a helper, and stores the resulting pointer in the structure. It loops over the table, and gives up after 21 attempts, clearing its state.

name: set_sign_from_helper_result
description: Calls a helper and sets a shared global word to one when it returns zero, otherwise to minus one.

name: store_table_offset_pointer
description: Calls a helper to obtain an index, then stores the structure base plus a table-stored offset into structure field 784.

name: store_indexed_table_word
description: Calls a helper to obtain an index, then stores the word at that index of the table into a shared global word.

name: store_second_table_pointer
description: Calls a helper to obtain an index, then stores the structure base plus a longword from the table into structure field 792.

name: call_two_routines_passthrough
description: Calls two subroutines in sequence and returns their register inputs unchanged. It is a pass-through with no logic of its own.

name: start_audio_channel_after_delay
description: When the flag at structure field 756 is zero and a channel's bit is already set in the shared word, runs a busy-wait loop of about 575 iterations. It then sets up that channel's pointer and length registers and writes its DMA and interrupt enable bits.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: When the buffer pointer is non-null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed structure area into it and then calls the routine supplied in another register. It returns nothing of its own.

name: build_max_sized_entry_buffer
description: Walks a linked list to find the largest stored size, starting from 149, then allocates a block sized to that maximum and fills it with a counting sequence. It copies sixteen longwords into the new structure and returns zero on success, or minus one when an allocation fails.

name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_invoke
description: Copies sixteen longwords from a fixed structure area into a buffer when the pointer is non-null, then invokes the routine given in another register. It duplicates the copy-and-call step of its neighbour.

name: parse_workbench_startup_arguments
description: Program entry point that finds its own task, opens the DOS and exec libraries, and reads the Workbench startup message. It splits the argument string into a list of words, honouring quoted strings and backslash escapes for newline and escape characters, then calls a cleanup routine before returning.

name: release_startup_resources_and_return
description: Stores a result value in a structure, then releases resources conditionally: closes the DOS library, closes the exec library, and replies to a message while multitasking is forbidden. It finishes by freeing the structure and returns the stored value.

name: launch_tool_from_workbench
description: Opens the required libraries, scans the startup arguments for a debug flag, and allocates a 160-byte buffer. It copies a stored string through two XOR passes with the same key, which leaves it unchanged, then starts the tool through library calls and calls a shutdown routine with the value 20 when a call fails.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings byte by byte, returning minus one when the first is smaller, one when it is larger, and zero when they are equal.

name: build_linked_list_from_table
description: Walks a table of pointer-linked entries, allocating an 8-byte node for each and storing a value from a library call in it. The new nodes are chained in order and the head is returned, stopping early if an allocation or value fails.

name: blank_version_suffix_on_match
description: Checks whether the character at offset 20 of the buffer is the digit 2 and matches the global string. When it does, it overwrites five bytes at offset 17 with a dot and spaces, matching the Workbench release text in the binary, and otherwise returns after the comparison.

name: write_dot_and_spaces_suffix
description: Writes a dot followed by four spaces into five consecutive bytes starting at offset 17 of the buffer. It is the write half of the version-text replacement in the neighbouring routine.

name: check_buffer_starts_with_global
description: Compares the buffer character by character with the global string and returns once the global string ends or a character differs. It has no return value, so the outcome is only visible through the caller.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return and performs no operation. It is entered through a callback slot that needs a valid target.

name: forward_with_stack_slot
description: Calls another routine passing its two parameters and the address of a stack slot in its frame, then returns. It is a thin forwarding wrapper.

name: format_stack_message_and_send
description: Calls exec.RawDoFmt to format a message into a 140-byte stack buffer, measures the zero-terminated length, and passes the buffer and length to a second routine when the length is non-zero. It is the formatted-output step of its caller.

name: process_amigados_hunk_records
description: Program entry of the port handler. It initialises a hunk record from a table, then walks a record list dispatching on AmigaDOS hunk type codes for code, data, relocation and external records, plus two access-flag codes, calling library routines between entries.

name: compare_block_bitmap_records
description: Program entry of the disk validator. It reads disk-block records through library calls, compares each bit of two stored bit arrays, and counts mismatches while walking chained ranges, calling helper routines for each mismatch.

name: copy_memory_then_dispatch
description: Program entry of the RAM handler. It calls exec.CopyMem through the exec library base, then transfers control through an unrecovered jump table.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler recovered no real code here, only bad instruction data, so control flow stops at once. The routine has no behaviour to describe.

name: reinit_serial_buffer_fields
description: Frees the block named by the second argument when it is set. When the size argument is non-zero it allocates a buffer of that size, then clears a set of unit fields and stores half-size and quarter-size values for buffer positions.

name: clear_request_flag_and_reply
description: Clears a status byte in the request, and when the status bits under a mask are all zero it replies to the request message through the exec library base.

name: toggle_serial_interrupt_bit
description: Writes the serial interrupt-enable bit off, calls a helper, then writes the bit back on. The write brackets the helper call so the interrupt is disabled only for its duration.

name: dequeue_serial_request
description: Removes a request from one of two linked queues, chosen by its command type, and clears its busy bits. If the request is still busy it returns; otherwise it replies to the message through the exec library.

name: unlink_request_from_first_queue
description: Unlinks the request from the first queue, clearing the queue head when the request is the head. It then marks the request done, and replies to its message through the exec library when it is not busy.

name: unlink_queued_request_if_flagged
description: When the request's flag bit is set, unlinks it from its queue and decrements the queue count. It then marks the request done and replies to its message when it is not busy.

name: clear_uart_break_and_unlink
description: Unlinks the request from its queue. For a request of its type with a pending flag, it clears the UART break bit in the audio control register, calls a helper, then marks the request done and replies when it is not busy.

name: unlink_second_queue_request
description: When the request's flag bit is set, unlinks it from the second queue and decrements that queue's count. It then marks the request done and replies to its message when it is not busy.

name: free_request_and_return_value
description: When a field of the request is set, marks it with a flag and returns zero. Otherwise it makes several library vector calls on the device structure, frees the request block, unlinks it from its list, and returns the saved value.

name: invoke_library_vectors_then_unlink
description: Calls several library vectors on the device structure, copies a word from the request to return, frees the request block, and unlinks it from its list. It has the same tail as its neighbour but omits the field check.

name: queue_request_or_reply
description: When the request's length field is non-zero, marks it as queued, appends it to the tail of a request list, increments the count and calls a library vector. Otherwise it replies to the message when it is not busy.

name: transmit_from_ring_buffer
description: When no request is active it dequeues the next pending request, then moves bytes from a circular buffer toward the serial output, handling wrap-around. It sets a status code on the request when the buffer runs out.

name: receive_serial_bytes_into_buffer
description: Moves received bytes into the caller's buffer, counting each one and honouring a mask of allowed characters with wrap-around in the ring buffer. It completes the read request when the requested count is reached.

name: finish_read_and_start_next
description: Stores the received byte and counts it, and when the request is complete it clears the active state, replies to the finished message through the exec library, and starts the next queued request.

name: finish_read_then_drain_queue
description: Clears the active state and replies to the finished message through the exec library when it is not busy. It then starts queued requests, after a helper call, until the queue is empty.

name: clear_bit_and_drain_queue
description: Clears one channel bit from the input value, stores the received bytes as its neighbours do, then clears the active state, replies when not busy, and starts the next queued request.

name: empty_interrupt_handler_stub
description: Contains only a return and performs no operation. It serves as a no-op target for an interrupt or callback slot.

name: set_request_error_and_drain
description: Sets the request's status code from the device's status flags, clears the active state, replies to the message when not busy, and starts the next queued request.

name: set_status_and_drain_next
description: Sets the request's status code from the device's status flags, then clears the active state and starts the next queued request, replying to the message when it is not busy.

name: set_default_status_and_drain
description: Sets a default status code on the request, changing it to a second code when a device flag is set, then clears the active state and starts the next queued request.

name: handle_serial_receive_interrupt
description: Acknowledges the serial receive interrupt request and reads the serial data register. It checks the break and parity flags, then passes the byte on to the request-completion logic.

name: store_received_byte_or_match
description: Compares the incoming byte with a stored match character. On a match it clears a match flag and writes the interrupt-enable value; otherwise it stores the byte in the ring buffer when there is room and calls a library vector.

name: store_byte_in_ring_buffer
description: When a status flag is set it marks the request as ready. Otherwise it stores the received byte in the ring buffer, records the end pointer when the buffer is full, and calls a library vector.

name: store_byte_if_error_clear
description: Stores the byte in the ring buffer when the error bit is clear, and otherwise marks the request ready. It then calls a library vector.

name: store_byte_unless_error_flagged
description: Checks a device flag and either marks the request ready or stores the byte in the ring buffer. It then calls a library vector.

name: mark_request_ready_and_signal
description: Sets the ready flag on the request, records the buffer pointer when it is unset, then calls a library vector to signal completion.

name: store_byte_and_signal
description: Stores the byte in the ring buffer while there is room, records the pointer when the buffer is full, and calls a library vector.

name: record_pointer_then_signal
description: Records the buffer pointer when it is unset, calls a helper, then calls a library vector to signal completion.

name: update_serial_control_state
description: Copies a control byte from the device structure, clears a state bit, and clears the matching bit in the control register when the mask is set. It writes the interrupt-enable value otherwise.

name: set_serial_control_bits
description: Copies a second control byte from the device structure, sets a state bit, and sets a bit in the control register when a mask is set. It writes the interrupt-enable value otherwise.

name: clear_serial_status_byte
description: Clears a status byte in the device structure and returns.

name: start_timed_request_once
description: When a pending flag is clear, sets it, resets a count field to ten less than the stored value, and calls a library vector on a second base. It then sets a status byte when that call returns a value.

name: mark_timeout_and_signal
description: If a pending flag was set and the masked global status is zero, it marks the request as expired, records its buffer pointer when that is unset, and calls a library vector.

name: filter_and_store_byte
description: Reads a value through a helper and masks it with a stored mask. When it matches the match character it sets or clears status bits; otherwise it stores the byte in the ring buffer and may call a library vector.

name: flag_pending_and_signal
description: Sets bit 0 of a status byte, records the buffer pointer when it is unset, and calls a library vector.

name: enqueue_or_start_request
description: Clears the request's count, then starts it immediately when the queue is empty and no timeout is pending, or appends it to a wait queue otherwise. It replies to the message when its status bits are clear.

name: start_queued_request_if_idle
description: When a device flag is set it runs a helper and replies to the message if the device is idle. Otherwise it marks the request active, records its buffer pointer, and writes the interrupt-enable value.

name: empty_handler_return
description: Contains only a return. It is an unused handler slot that does nothing when called.

name: set_status_if_break_bits
description: When two status masks both match, sets the request's status code to 13. It does nothing otherwise.

name: dequeue_next_request_and_start
description: Handles a pending status byte first. Otherwise it dequeues the next waiting request when the active queue allows, updates the queue count, sets the state bits, and starts the request.

name: transmit_next_byte_from_request
description: Sets a fixed timeout of 200, reads the next byte from the request buffer, and masks it against a status word. It updates the status register and advances the buffer pointer and counter while within the request's count.

name: receive_byte_with_mask_check
description: Once a count limit is passed, merges the incoming byte with a status-bit mask, then advances the counter. It checks the byte against the stored match character and stores the status for the request.

name: complete_read_when_limit_reached
description: Reads the serial data value, merges in a status bit, and advances the counters. It completes the request, clearing its flag and replying through the exec library, when the match character or count limit is reached.

name: dequeue_request_if_queued
description: When the second queue holds requests, unlinks the next one, resets its count and timer fields, and sets its status bits. A request of one type triggers a helper call; with an empty queue it sets the shared global word to one instead.

name: set_status_word_to_one
description: Sets the shared global status word to one and returns.

name: combine_pending_status_byte
description: Takes a pending status byte, clears it, merges it into the shared status word, and resets that word to one when both queues are empty.

name: reset_serial_device_defaults
description: Disables serial interrupts, clears any queued requests, then stores the default unit parameters, including a 9600 value and a value of 250000. It re-enables the interrupt and replies to the message when the device is idle.

name: forward_then_reply_if_idle
description: Calls a helper, then replies to the message through the exec library when the device is idle.

name: flag_queue_then_reply
description: Sets a pending flag when the first queue is non-empty, calls a helper when the second queue has an entry, and replies to the message when the device is idle. It returns the helper's value.

name: clear_flag_then_reply
description: Clears a pending flag, calls a helper when the first queue has an entry, sets the shared global word to the enable value, and replies to the message when the device is idle.

name: helper_between_interrupt_writes
description: Disables the serial interrupt bit, calls a helper, then re-enables it. It replies to the message through the exec library when the device is idle.

name: drain_list_calling_helper
description: Repeatedly removes the head entry of a list and calls a helper on it until the list is empty.

name: stub_no_operation
description: Contains only a return and does nothing when called.

name: capture_cia_status_and_reply
description: Reads a CIA status byte, masks it, and merges in a flag bit when the device flags are set. It stores the status and timer value in the request, clears a pending bit, and replies to the message when the device is idle.

name: queue_or_activate_request
description: Enqueues the request when the device has pending work. Otherwise it calls a helper and either makes the request active with a control-register write, or replies to it when the helper reports a failure.

name: activate_request_after_helper
description: Calls a helper, then makes the request active and writes the control value when its status is clear. Otherwise it clears the active request and replies to the message through the exec library.

name: reply_and_clear_active_request
description: Replies to the message through the exec library and clears the active request field.

name: clear_uart_break_and_reply
description: When a pending flag is set and the active request has one type, it clears the active request and the UART break bit in the control register, replies to the message, and writes the enable value.

name: start_timed_read_request
description: Sets the shared global word to one, clears the request's timer fields, and sets a count to nine. It then calls a library vector and sets a status byte when the call returns a non-zero result.

name: update_device_flag_and_restart
description: Sets or clears a device flag from the request. When no queued work is pending it writes the interrupt-enable bracket around a helper call, otherwise it sets a status byte, then replies to the message when idle.

name: clear_flag_and_restart_idle
description: Clears a device flag, then when no queued work is pending writes the interrupt-enable bracket around a helper call, otherwise it sets a status byte. It replies to the message when idle.

name: bracket_helper_then_reply_idle
description: Disables the serial interrupt bit, calls a helper, re-enables the bit, then replies to the message through the exec library when the device is idle.

name: validate_serial_unit_parameters
description: Checks the requested unit parameters against fixed ranges, including a 32-bit value that must fall between 111 and 292001. It copies the accepted values into the device structure and sets flags from the request, returning without change when a check fails.

name: compute_unit_channel_masks
description: Builds a one-bit channel mask from the unit number, doubling it for one unit type and shifting it for a flag. It stores the mask in the device structure and then calls two helpers to store two results.

name: set_status_code_five
description: Sets the request's status byte to five.

name: compute_serial_period_divisor
description: Multiplies a stored value by seven and divides a fixed value of 25000000 by the product, with a scaling branch for large products. It stores the 16-bit quotient in the device structure and sets a flag when the unit matches and a bit is set.

name: store_serial_period_quotient
description: Divides an input value by a 16-bit divisor and stores the quotient as the device period. It sets a flag when the unit matches and a bit is set, and the serial period register is written through the device structure.

name: open_misc_and_init_device
description: Allocates the device structure through a library call and stores the caller's argument in it. It opens the misc resource through the exec library, and on success initialises the queue fields, the timer, and the handler pointers in the structure.

name: initialise_serial_queue_heads
description: Points two queue heads at their own structure offsets and sets two entries to the value five. It stores the handler pointers, calls a library vector, writes the interrupt-enable value, and returns one.

name: fill_request_block_fields
description: Fills a request block by storing a pointer to the shared global word, setting its type byte to 16, and copying two longword values into the block.

name: init_queues_and_set_request
description: Initialises the two serial queues and their entries in the same way as its neighbour, calls a library vector, and sets the shared global word to the enable value. It returns one.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Returns zero and performs no other action.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler recovered only bad instruction data here, so control flow stops at once. The keymap file contains no executable code to describe.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler recovered only bad instruction data here, so control flow stops at once. The sound data file holds no routine behaviour to describe.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler recovered only bad instruction data here, so control flow stops at once. The sound data file holds no routine behaviour to describe.

name: increment_count_and_clear_flag
description: Increments a 16-bit count at one structure offset and clears one bit in a flag byte in the same structure. This is library code in the shared icon library, not game code.

name: decrement_count_and_release
description: Decrements the 16-bit count in the library structure. When the count reaches zero and a pending flag bit is set, it calls a release helper and returns its result, otherwise it returns zero.

name: free_structure_or_mark_pending
description: When the count field is zero, frees the library structure through the exec library and unlinks it from its list. Otherwise it sets a pending bit in the flag byte and returns zero.

name: set_pending_flag_return_zero
description: Sets a pending bit in a flag byte of the library structure and returns zero.

name: return_zero_no_action
description: Returns zero with no other action, in the icon library's routine table.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Stores its arguments in a structure, opens dos.library through the exec library, and records the library base in two shared fields on success. On failure it raises an alert through the exec library.

name: copy_longs_to_shared_slots
description: Copies two longword fields from the structure at register A2 into two shared global slots. This is library code in the shared icon library.

name: forward_to_slot_helper
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub with no logic of its own, entered from several library vector slots.

name: forward_to_vector_helper
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub with no logic of its own, entered from the library vector table.

name: call_helper_then_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns, with no logic of its own. Its behaviour is that of the routine it reaches.

name: call_helper_unconditionally
description: Makes an unconditional call to one other routine and then returns. No arguments are set up here.

name: call_helper_at_entry
description: Calls one other routine at entry and returns. It has no conditions, so its effect is whatever the called routine does.

name: call_helper_from_table_entry
description: Calls one other routine from a table entry and returns. The stub adds no logic of its own.

name: call_helper_from_vector_slot
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub reached from a library vector slot.

name: call_helper_from_handler_slot
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub reached from a handler slot in the data.

name: call_helper_from_pointer_slot
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub reached through a pointer slot in the data.

name: call_helper_from_init_slot
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: relay_call_to_helper
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: pass_call_to_helper
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: forward_call_then_return
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: forward_call_to_helper
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: chain_call_to_helper
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: store_value_in_returned_record
description: Calls a library vector on the library base with its first argument, then stores its second argument at offset 148 in the record that call returns. This is library code in the shared icon library.

name: call_pair_undo_on_failure
description: Calls a routine with its last two arguments and, if that returns non-zero, calls a second routine with the result. When the second call fails it calls a cleanup routine on the first result and returns zero.

name: copy_stack_record_into_structure
description: Looks up a structure from its first argument, reads a 44-byte record from the stack into the structure at offset 96, and copies several fields from the stack into their structure offsets. It returns the structure when the lookup succeeds.

name: copy_frame_fields_into_structure
description: Copies a 44-byte block and several fields from the frame into the structure at register A2, then links the structure's back pointer when one is set. It is the frame-to-structure copy used by its caller.

name: return_zero_library_stub
description: Returns zero immediately with no other action. It is a library stub in the shared icon library.

name: build_header_record_and_call
description: Builds a header record on the stack holding a fixed tag value and version 1, copies 44 bytes and several fields from the structure into it, then passes the record to another routine. This is library code in the shared icon library.

name: load_icon_info_record
description: Builds a path in a 260-byte stack buffer, looks up the .info file, and reads its record through library calls. It validates the tag and version and fills in the icon structure's fields, allocating sub-blocks when needed.

name: validate_icon_record_fields
description: Checks the record's tag and version, clears two fields, then processes optional sub-blocks through library calls. It returns one on success.

name: read_icon_optional_blocks
description: Allocates and reads optional blocks through library calls at several offsets, storing their pointers in the structure. It returns one when all reads succeed.

name: copy_longs_until_count_exhausted
description: Copies 4-byte values from a source into a destination array through library calls until the remaining byte count is used up. It then reads one more value and returns one on success or zero on failure.

name: call_helper_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine and returns zero. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library.

name: empty_return_stub
description: Contains only a return and performs no operation.

name: allocate_icon_record_buffer
description: Allocates a 260-byte buffer through a library call. On allocation failure it calls a routine with error code 103 and returns zero; otherwise it copies the arguments, reads a pair of records, and returns the buffer when the checks succeed.

name: read_icon_info_fields
description: Reads header words from the structure, makes library reads through the library base for the .info file, and returns one when the reads succeed.

name: write_icon_string_list_records
description: Writes a count record, then walks a zero-terminated pointer list and writes each entry through library calls. It writes an optional trailing value when set and returns one on success.

name: measure_pointer_list_length
description: Measures a zero-terminated pointer list by counting its length, then writes each entry through library calls and an optional trailing value. It records the final count in the structure and returns the status.

name: write_pointer_list_entries
description: Walks a zero-terminated pointer list, writing each entry's record through library calls and an optional trailing value. It records the final count in the structure and returns the status.

name: drain_icon_list_entries
description: Repeatedly calls one routine on a field of the structure and passes each non-zero result to another routine, until the first returns zero.

name: no_op_return_stub
description: Contains only a return and performs no operation.

name: forward_call_at_offset_140
description: Calls one routine with the first argument and the structure address advanced by 140 bytes, then returns.

name: allocate_and_initialise_icon_block
description: Allocates a 168-byte cleared block through a library call and calls a routine on its interior at offset 142. It returns the block on success, and on failure releases it and returns zero.

name: tail_call_helper_stub
description: Calls one other routine and returns. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library, with no logic of its own.

name: return_zero_stub_icon
description: Returns zero with no other action. It is a stub in the shared icon library.

name: append_pair_to_table
description: Decrements a count, growing the table through a routine when it is exhausted, then stores two values as a pair in the table and returns one. It returns zero when the growth fails.

name: store_pair_after_decrement
description: Decrements a short count through a pointer, stores two register values as a pair at the decremented index in the table, and returns one.

name: allocate_and_fill_record_block
description: Allocates a 94-byte cleared block through a library call, calls routines on its fields in turn, and returns the block on success. Otherwise it releases the block and returns zero.

name: stub_return_only_icon
description: Contains only a return and performs no operation. It is a stub in the shared icon library.

name: call_then_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine through the library and returns zero. It is a single-call stub in the shared icon library.

name: forward_call_at_offset_78
description: Calls one routine with the first argument and the structure address advanced by 78 bytes, then returns.

name: find_key_value_in_list
description: Walks a zero-terminated list of strings, comparing each entry through a helper and checking for an equals sign after the match. It returns a pointer to the value that follows the key, or zero when no entry matches.

name: return_zero_stub_icon
description: Returns zero with no other action. It is a stub in the shared icon library.

name: scan_entries_for_match
description: Walks a list of entries separated by the pipe character, comparing each one through library calls. It returns one when a match checks out and zero when the list ends.

name: find_matching_delimited_entry
description: Walks entries separated by the pipe character, comparing each one through a helper against a target value. It returns one when a match is found and zero at the end of the list.

name: find_delimited_entry_by_length
description: Walks entries separated by the pipe character, comparing each entry's length against a target length and checking a follow-up call. It returns one when an entry matches and zero when the entries end.

name: search_delimited_entries_by_length
description: Walks entries separated by the pipe character, comparing each entry's length against a target. It returns one on a match and zero when the list is exhausted.

name: return_zero_stub_icon
description: Returns zero with no other action. It is a stub in the shared icon library.

name: format_copy_title_with_number
description: Parses a short decimal count at offset 5 and writes a title beginning with copy or copy of into a 30-byte name field. It then appends the remaining text and returns the structure.

name: parse_copy_count_field
description: Parses a 3-digit copy count at offset 5 and, when the count is valid, copies a further name field. Otherwise it copies a default name, and it makes two library-style calls either way.

name: parse_decimal_prefix
description: Parses decimal digits from a pointer until a non-digit appears, then checks the following four characters through a helper. It makes two further calls before returning.

name: format_copy_message_from_digits
description: Parses a decimal count from the text, checks the following characters through a helper, then calls routines to format and output a copy message using a copy-of format string.

name: decode_decimal_digit
description: Returns the value of a character when it is in the range zero to nine, otherwise minus one.

name: call_allocmem_vector
description: Calls the library vector at minus 198 through a library base pointer stored in a shared slot. It is the allocate-memory entry for the icon library.

name: call_pair_undo_on_failure
description: Calls a routine with its last two arguments and, if that returns non-zero, calls a second routine with the result. When the second call fails it calls a cleanup routine on the first result and returns zero.

name: allocate_96_byte_cleared_block
description: Allocates a 96-byte cleared block through a library call, sets two of its fields to ten, and stores a pointer to the block in a parameter array. It returns true when the allocation succeeded.
